# Introduction

Clinical programs are full of **process rules with memory**. A subject
is screening, then eligible, then randomized, then on treatment — or
screen-failed. A dose continues, reduces, holds, or stops depending on
toxicity *and* how many holds already happened. A visit is scheduled,
open in window, completed, or missed.

Those rules are often written as nested `if` / `else` (or a giant
`dplyr::case_when`). That works for a one-shot classification of a
static row. It ages badly once the *current state* matters, illegal
paths must be rejected, and auditors ask which transitions fired.

A **finite-state machine** (FSM) makes the process explicit:

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| **State** | Where the subject / dose / visit is now |
| **Event** | What happened (pass screen, grade 3 AE, window day) |
| **Transition** | Legal move `from + event → to` |
| **Guard** | Optional predicate on context (grade, labs, counters) |
| **Action** | Optional side effect (log, set next dose, raise QC flag) |

> Encode *allowed* clinical paths as data. Drive decisions by looking
> up `(state, event)` — do not re-walk a decision tree on every call.

This article builds a small table-driven FSM in R, rewrites a nested
disposition script and a dose-modification policy, and shows a short
visit-readiness machine. The focus is **deterministic** protocol logic.

**Not the same as Viterbi / HMM.** Reconstructing a *latent* RECIST-like
path under missing visits is a probabilistic decoding problem — see the
companion post on Viterbi decoding. An FSM here is a **protocol
decision engine**: given the current official state and an event, what
is the next official state? Illegal transitions fail loudly.

```{r}
#| label: packages
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
```

# Motivation

## Nested disposition logic

A common first draft for subject disposition looks like this:

```{r}
#| label: disposition-ifelse
#| eval: false
update_disposition <- function(status, event) {
  if (status == "Screening") {
    if (event == "pass_screen") {
      "Eligible"
    } else if (event == "fail_screen") {
      "ScreenFail"
    } else {
      stop("illegal")
    }
  } else if (status == "Eligible") {
    if (event == "randomize") {
      "Randomized"
    } else if (event == "fail_screen") {
      "ScreenFail"
    } else {
      stop("illegal")
    }
  } else if (status == "Randomized") {
    if (event == "start_tx") {
      "OnTreatment"
    } else if (event == "discontinue") {
      "Discontinued"
    } else {
      stop("illegal")
    }
  } else if (status == "OnTreatment") {
    if (event == "complete") {
      "Completed"
    } else if (event == "discontinue") {
      "Discontinued"
    } else {
      stop("illegal")
    }
  } else {
    stop("terminal or unknown status")
  }
}
```

Every new status or event adds another nest. Illegal paths are easy to
miss (`Randomized` + `pass_screen`). Terminal states are easy to forget.
Unit tests must re-encode the same tree. Reviewers cannot *see* the
allowed graph without simulating every branch.

## Dose modification with memory

Dose rules usually depend on **history**, not only the latest grade:

```{r}
#| label: dose-ifelse-sketch
#| eval: false
# grade 1 → continue
# grade 2 → reduce once, else hold
# grade 3 → hold; after 2 holds → discontinue
# grade 4 → discontinue
# ...plus: no action while already Holding unless resume/discontinue
```

Nested conditionals mix *state* (`OnDose`, `Holding`, `Reduced`,
`Discontinued`), *event* (new toxicity grade, resume, permanent stop),
and *context* (`n_holds`, `current_dose`). The FSM separates those
concerns.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: ifelse-vs-fsm
%%| fig-width: 6.2
%%| out-width: "100%"
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"rankSpacing": 24, "nodeSpacing": 14, "padding": 6}}}%%
flowchart LR
  subgraph tangled [NestedIfElse]
    direction TB
    s1[status] --> deep[DeepBranches]
    e1[event] --> deep
  end
  subgraph machine [TableDrivenFSM]
    direction TB
    st[state] --> tbl[transitionTable]
    ev[event] --> tbl
    tbl --> nx[nextState]
  end
  tangled ~~~ machine
```

| Nearby idea | Role |
|---|---|
| `case_when` on one snapshot | Fine for ADaM recodes with no process memory |
| Nested `if` / `else` | Encodes the graph in control flow; hard to audit |
| Deterministic FSM | Explicit legal graph; rejects illegal moves |
| HMM + Viterbi | Most probable *latent* path under noise / missingness |

# Mechanics in R

## Transition table and engine

States and events are character labels. Transitions live in a tibble.
Guards and actions are ordinary R functions of a **context** list
(mutable counters, dose, QC notes).

```{r}
#| label: fsm-engine
new_fsm <- function(states, events, transitions, initial) {
  stopifnot(initial %in% states)
  tr <- as_tibble(transitions)
  need <- c("from", "event", "to")
  stopifnot(all(need %in% names(tr)))
  if (!"guard" %in% names(tr)) {
    tr$guard <- vector("list", nrow(tr))
  }
  if (!"action" %in% names(tr)) {
    tr$action <- vector("list", nrow(tr))
  }
  tr <- tr |>
    mutate(
      guard = map(guard, ~ if (is.null(.x)) function(ctx) TRUE else .x),
      action = map(action, ~ if (is.null(.x)) function(ctx) ctx else .x)
    )
  structure(
    list(
      states = unique(states),
      events = unique(events),
      transitions = tr,
      initial = initial
    ),
    class = "clinical_fsm"
  )
}

step_fsm <- function(machine, state, event, context = list()) {
  stopifnot(inherits(machine, "clinical_fsm"))
  if (!state %in% machine$states) {
    stop(sprintf("Unknown state '%s'.", state), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!event %in% machine$events) {
    stop(sprintf("Unknown event '%s'.", event), call. = FALSE)
  }

  # `.env$event` is required: `event` is also a column, so a bare
  # `event` on the RHS would compare the column to itself.
  cands <- machine$transitions |>
    filter(.data$from == .env$state, .data$event == .env$event)

  if (nrow(cands) == 0L) {
    stop(
      sprintf("Illegal transition: %s + %s.", state, event),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cands))) {
    row <- cands[i, ]
    guard <- row$guard[[1]]
    if (isTRUE(guard(context))) {
      action <- row$action[[1]]
      new_ctx <- action(context)
      return(list(
        state = row$to[[1]],
        context = new_ctx,
        fired = TRUE
      ))
    }
  }

  stop(
    sprintf("No guard passed for %s + %s.", state, event),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

run_fsm <- function(machine, events, context = list(),
                    start = machine$initial) {
  state <- start
  history <- tibble(
    step = integer(),
    from = character(),
    event = character(),
    to = character()
  )
  for (k in seq_along(events)) {
    ev <- events[[k]]
    out <- step_fsm(machine, state, ev, context)
    history <- bind_rows(
      history,
      tibble(step = k, from = state, event = ev, to = out$state)
    )
    state <- out$state
    context <- out$context
  }
  list(state = state, context = context, history = history)
}

print.clinical_fsm <- function(x, ...) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "clinical_fsm: %d states, %d events, %d transitions (start = %s)\n",
    length(x$states), length(x$events), nrow(x$transitions), x$initial
  ))
  invisible(x)
}
```

The engine is deliberately small: **lookup**, **guard**, **action**,
**reject**. Clinical meaning lives in the table, not in a growing
`if` ladder.

# Example A: subject disposition

## Allowed graph

```{mermaid}
%%| label: disposition-graph
%%| fig-width: 5.8
%%| out-width: "100%"
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Screening
  Screening --> Eligible: pass_screen
  Screening --> ScreenFail: fail_screen
  Eligible --> Randomized: randomize
  Eligible --> ScreenFail: fail_screen
  Randomized --> OnTreatment: start_tx
  Randomized --> Discontinued: discontinue
  OnTreatment --> Completed: complete
  OnTreatment --> Discontinued: discontinue
```

```{r}
#| label: disposition-fsm
disp_states <- c(
  "Screening", "Eligible", "Randomized", "OnTreatment",
  "Completed", "Discontinued", "ScreenFail"
)
disp_events <- c(
  "pass_screen", "fail_screen", "randomize",
  "start_tx", "complete", "discontinue"
)

disp_tr <- tribble(
  ~from,         ~event,         ~to,
  "Screening",   "pass_screen",  "Eligible",
  "Screening",   "fail_screen",  "ScreenFail",
  "Eligible",    "randomize",    "Randomized",
  "Eligible",    "fail_screen",  "ScreenFail",
  "Randomized",  "start_tx",     "OnTreatment",
  "Randomized",  "discontinue",  "Discontinued",
  "OnTreatment", "complete",     "Completed",
  "OnTreatment", "discontinue",  "Discontinued"
)

disposition_fsm <- new_fsm(
  states = disp_states,
  events = disp_events,
  transitions = disp_tr,
  initial = "Screening"
)
disposition_fsm
```

## Same paths as the nested function — as data

```{r}
#| label: disposition-runs
path_ok <- run_fsm(
  disposition_fsm,
  c("pass_screen", "randomize", "start_tx", "complete")
)
path_ok$history
path_ok$state

path_sf <- run_fsm(
  disposition_fsm,
  c("pass_screen", "fail_screen")
)
path_sf$history
path_sf$state
```

Illegal moves fail instead of silently falling through an `else`:

```{r}
#| label: disposition-illegal
#| error: true
step_fsm(disposition_fsm, "ScreenFail", "start_tx")
```

```{r}
#| label: disposition-illegal-2
#| error: true
step_fsm(disposition_fsm, "Randomized", "pass_screen")
```

## Many subjects, one machine

Event logs become ordinary tidy data. The machine is applied per
subject:

```{r}
#| label: disposition-cohort
event_log <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID, ~seq, ~event,
  "S-001", 1, "pass_screen",
  "S-001", 2, "randomize",
  "S-001", 3, "start_tx",
  "S-001", 4, "complete",
  "S-002", 1, "fail_screen",
  "S-003", 1, "pass_screen",
  "S-003", 2, "randomize",
  "S-003", 3, "discontinue"
)

# S-001 Screening → Eligible → Randomized → OnTreatment → Completed
# S-002 Screening → ScreenFail
# S-003 Screening → Eligible → Randomized → Discontinued
#       (withdrew after randomization, before first dose)
expected <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID, ~FINAL_STATUS, ~N_EVENTS,
  "S-001",  "Completed",          4L,
  "S-002",  "ScreenFail",         1L,
  "S-003",  "Discontinued",       3L
)

final_disp <- event_log |>
  arrange(USUBJID, seq) |>
  group_by(USUBJID) |>
  group_modify(function(df, key) {
    out <- run_fsm(disposition_fsm, df$event)
    tibble(
      FINAL_STATUS = out$state,
      N_EVENTS = nrow(out$history)
    )
  }) |>
  ungroup()

final_disp
stopifnot(identical(
  final_disp[, c("USUBJID", "FINAL_STATUS", "N_EVENTS")],
  expected
))
```

Compared with nested `if`s, adding `Randomized → ScreenFail` (late
discovery of eligibility failure) adds **one row** to `disp_tr`; the
engine, the callers, and the replay loop stay untouched.

# Example B: dose modification as decision-making

A simplified oncology-style policy (illustrative — not a real SAP):

- States: `OnDose`, `Reduced`, `Holding`, `Discontinued`
- Start at full dose 100
- Toxicity events carry a CTCAE-like `grade` in context
- Resume from hold returns to the last active dosing state
- Two completed holds → discontinue on the next hold-worthy event
- Grade ≤ 2 while `Holding` → stay in `Holding` (no new action)

```{r}
#| label: dose-fsm
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

always <- function(ctx) TRUE
grade_le <- function(g) function(ctx) !is.null(ctx$grade) && ctx$grade <= g
grade_eq <- function(g) function(ctx) isTRUE(ctx$grade == g)
grade_ge <- function(g) function(ctx) !is.null(ctx$grade) && ctx$grade >= g

continue_dose <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$last_action <- "continue"
  ctx
}

reduce_dose <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$dose <- max(ctx$dose * 0.75, 25)
  ctx$last_action <- "reduce"
  ctx$active <- "Reduced"
  ctx
}

start_hold <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$n_holds <- ctx$n_holds + 1L
  ctx$last_action <- "hold"
  ctx
}

resume_dose <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$last_action <- "resume"
  ctx
}

stop_tx <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$dose <- 0
  ctx$last_action <- "discontinue"
  ctx
}

holds_lt <- function(n) function(ctx) isTRUE(ctx$n_holds < n)
holds_ge <- function(n) function(ctx) isTRUE(ctx$n_holds >= n)

max_holds <- 2L

stay_holding <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$last_action <- "stay"
  ctx
}

dose_states <- c("OnDose", "Reduced", "Holding", "Discontinued")
dose_events <- c("tox", "resume", "permanent_stop")

# Multiple rows per (from, event): first matching guard wins.
# Built with tibble() so guards/actions stay as list-columns of functions.
dose_tr <- tibble::tibble(
  from = c(
    "OnDose", "OnDose", "OnDose", "OnDose", "OnDose", "OnDose",
    "Reduced", "Reduced", "Reduced", "Reduced", "Reduced",
    "Holding", "Holding", "Holding", "Holding", "Holding"
  ),
  event = c(
    "tox", "tox", "tox", "tox", "tox", "permanent_stop",
    "tox", "tox", "tox", "tox", "permanent_stop",
    "resume", "resume", "tox", "tox", "permanent_stop"
  ),
  to = c(
    "OnDose", "Reduced", "Holding", "Discontinued", "Discontinued",
    "Discontinued",
    "Reduced", "Holding", "Discontinued", "Discontinued", "Discontinued",
    "OnDose", "Reduced", "Holding", "Discontinued", "Discontinued"
  ),
  guard = list(
    grade_le(1),
    grade_eq(2),
    function(ctx) grade_eq(3)(ctx) && holds_lt(max_holds)(ctx),
    function(ctx) grade_eq(3)(ctx) && holds_ge(max_holds)(ctx),
    grade_ge(4),
    always,
    grade_le(1),
    function(ctx) {
      (grade_eq(2)(ctx) || grade_eq(3)(ctx)) && holds_lt(max_holds)(ctx)
    },
    function(ctx) {
      (grade_eq(2)(ctx) || grade_eq(3)(ctx)) && holds_ge(max_holds)(ctx)
    },
    grade_ge(4),
    always,
    function(ctx) identical(ctx$active %||% "OnDose", "OnDose"),
    function(ctx) identical(ctx$active, "Reduced"),
    grade_le(2),
    grade_ge(3),
    always
  ),
  action = list(
    continue_dose, reduce_dose, start_hold, stop_tx, stop_tx, stop_tx,
    continue_dose, start_hold, stop_tx, stop_tx, stop_tx,
    resume_dose, resume_dose, stay_holding, stop_tx, stop_tx
  )
)

dose_fsm <- new_fsm(
  states = dose_states,
  events = dose_events,
  transitions = dose_tr,
  initial = "OnDose"
)
```
## Walk a toxicity timeline

```{r}
#| label: dose-walk
ctx0 <- list(
  dose = 100,
  n_holds = 0L,
  active = "OnDose",
  last_action = NA_character_,
  grade = NA_integer_
)

apply_tox <- function(machine, state, context, grade) {
  context$grade <- grade
  step_fsm(machine, state, "tox", context)
}

# Grade 1 while on full dose → continue
s1 <- apply_tox(dose_fsm, "OnDose", ctx0, 1L)
s1$state
s1$context$dose
s1$context$last_action

# Grade 2 → reduce
s2 <- apply_tox(dose_fsm, s1$state, s1$context, 2L)
s2$state
s2$context$dose

# Grade 3 → first hold
s3 <- apply_tox(dose_fsm, s2$state, s2$context, 3L)
s3$state
s3$context$n_holds

# Resume to Reduced (active remembered)
s4 <- step_fsm(dose_fsm, s3$state, "resume", s3$context)
s4$state
s4$context$dose

# Another grade 3 → second hold
s5 <- apply_tox(dose_fsm, s4$state, s4$context, 3L)
s5$state
s5$context$n_holds

# Resume again, then grade 3 with n_holds >= 2 → discontinue
s6 <- step_fsm(dose_fsm, s5$state, "resume", s5$context)
s7 <- apply_tox(dose_fsm, s6$state, s6$context, 3L)
s7$state
s7$context$dose
s7$context$last_action
```

The nested `if` version would bury `n_holds`, `active`, and grade
thresholds inside each status branch. Here the **policy is the table**:
reviewers can read every legal `(state, event, guard) → to` line. Changing
“discontinue after two holds” to three is one edit to `max_holds`, not
surgery inside nested blocks.

## Audit trail for a subject

```{r}
#| label: dose-audit
simulate_dose <- function(grades) {
  state <- dose_fsm$initial
  context <- ctx0
  rows <- list()
  for (i in seq_along(grades)) {
    g <- grades[[i]]
    if (is.na(g)) {
      out <- step_fsm(dose_fsm, state, "resume", context)
      ev <- "resume"
    } else {
      context$grade <- g
      out <- step_fsm(dose_fsm, state, "tox", context)
      ev <- "tox"
    }
    rows[[i]] <- tibble(
      step = i,
      event = ev,
      grade = g,
      from = state,
      to = out$state,
      dose = out$context$dose,
      n_holds = out$context$n_holds,
      action = out$context$last_action
    )
    state <- out$state
    context <- out$context
  }
  bind_rows(rows)
}

# grades with NA = resume after hold
simulate_dose(c(1L, 2L, 3L, NA, 3L, NA, 3L))
```

# Example C: visit readiness

A lighter machine for attendance / window logic — useful when deriving
visit status flags without another `if` cascade in the ADaM step.

```{r}
#| label: visit-fsm
in_window <- function(ctx) {
  !is.null(ctx$study_day) &&
    ctx$study_day >= ctx$window_lo &&
    ctx$study_day <= ctx$window_hi
}
before_window <- function(ctx) {
  !is.null(ctx$study_day) && ctx$study_day < ctx$window_lo
}
after_window <- function(ctx) {
  !is.null(ctx$study_day) && ctx$study_day > ctx$window_hi
}

mark_missed <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$flag <- "missed_window"
  ctx
}
mark_done <- function(ctx) {
  ctx$flag <- "completed"
  ctx
}
identity_ctx <- function(ctx) ctx

visit_tr <- tibble::tibble(
  from = c(
    "Scheduled", "Scheduled", "Scheduled",
    "WindowOpen", "WindowOpen", "WindowOpen",
    "Scheduled"
  ),
  event = c("tick", "tick", "tick", "tick", "tick", "done", "done"),
  to = c(
    "Scheduled", "WindowOpen", "Missed",
    "WindowOpen", "Missed", "Done", "Done"
  ),
  guard = list(
    before_window, in_window, after_window,
    in_window, after_window, always, in_window
  ),
  action = list(
    identity_ctx, identity_ctx, mark_missed,
    identity_ctx, mark_missed, mark_done, mark_done
  )
)

visit_fsm <- new_fsm(
  states = c("Scheduled", "WindowOpen", "Done", "Missed"),
  events = c("tick", "done"),
  transitions = visit_tr,
  initial = "Scheduled"
)

# Week 4 window [25, 31]; subject arrives day 28
vctx <- list(study_day = 28, window_lo = 25, window_hi = 31, flag = NA_character_)
v1 <- step_fsm(visit_fsm, "Scheduled", "tick", vctx)
v2 <- step_fsm(visit_fsm, v1$state, "done", v1$context)
v2$state
v2$context$flag

# Subject never shows up: day 40 while still Scheduled → Missed
vmiss <- step_fsm(
  visit_fsm,
  "Scheduled",
  "tick",
  list(study_day = 40, window_lo = 25, window_hi = 31, flag = NA_character_)
)
vmiss$state
vmiss$context$flag
```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: visit-graph
%%| fig-width: 5.4
%%| out-width: "90%"
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Scheduled
  Scheduled --> Scheduled: tick before window
  Scheduled --> WindowOpen: tick in window
  Scheduled --> Done: done in window
  Scheduled --> Missed: tick after window
  WindowOpen --> WindowOpen: tick in window
  WindowOpen --> Done: done
  WindowOpen --> Missed: tick after window
```

# Pattern shape in clinical code

Practical placement:

1. **SAP / protocol** defines the allowed graph (human text + diagram).
2. **Transition table** is the machine-readable SAP fragment.
3. **Event log** (disposition events, toxicity grades, visit ticks)
   drives `run_fsm` / `step_fsm`.
4. **ADaM** stores the resulting status / dose / visit flag — and
   optionally the history for traceability.

The FSM does not replace tidy verbs for plain merges and summaries. It
replaces the *process kernel* that otherwise becomes nested control flow.

# When not to use a state machine

- Flat, memory-free recodes (`SEX`, `ARMN`, severity → numeric) —
  prefer `case_when`, formats, or a lookup table.
- A single branching rule with no recurring state — a plain function
  is clearer.
- Reconstructing latent disease course under missing assessments —
  use HMM / Viterbi (companion article), not a protocol FSM.
- Forcing every `if` in a reporting script into states — overkill;
  reserve FSMs for processes with illegal paths and history.

# Closing

| Situation | Prefer |
|---|---|
| Disposition / enrollment process | Table-driven FSM + event log |
| Dose modification with counters | FSM with guards and actions |
| Visit window readiness | Small FSM or explicit window functions |
| One-shot ADaM derivation | `case_when` / joins / formats |
| Latent path under missing visits | HMM + Viterbi |

# Summary

Clinical decision rules with memory — disposition, dosing, visit
readiness — are state machines whether the code admits it or not.
Nested `if` / `else` hides the allowed graph inside control flow. A
table-driven FSM in R surfaces **states**, **events**, **guards**, and
**actions** as data: illegal transitions fail loudly, policies become
reviewable rows, and cohort event logs replay through one engine.

Use an FSM when the protocol defines a process with illegal paths and
history. Prefer ordinary tidy recodes when there is no process memory,
and probabilistic decoders when the question is the most likely latent
chain rather than the next official state.

# References

- Gamma, E., Helm, R., Johnson, R., and Vlissides, J. (1994).
  *Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software*.
  Addison-Wesley. (State pattern.)
- Harel, D. (1987). Statecharts: A visual formalism for complex
  systems. *Science of Computer Programming*, 8(3), 231–274.
- ICH E9(R1) (2019). *Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis
  in Clinical Trials*. An FSM implements operational rules; it does
  not define the estimand.
- Companion post: Viterbi decoding for clinical response chains
  (HMM / latent paths under missing visits).
